name: Panettone
story: Milan’s lofty Christmas bread, enriched with butter, candied citrus and raisins.
steps: Mix flour, sugar, yeast, eggs and milk; knead until stretchy.
Knead in soft butter, raisins and peel; let rise until doubled.
Place in a tall mould and allow to rise again.
Bake at 170°C for 40–55 minutes; cool thoroughly.
tip: This is a home-style adaptation of traditional long-fermented panettone.

name: Pandoro
story: Verona’s golden, star-shaped buttery cake is finished with powdered sugar.
steps: Knead flour, yeast, sugar, eggs and milk into a soft dough.
Work in butter gradually and let rise until doubled.
Proof in a buttered star-shaped mould until puffy.
Bake at 170°C for 35–45 minutes; cool and dust with sugar.
tip: A simplified home dough rather than the classic multi-stage pastry method.

name: Struffoli
story: Neapolitan fried pastry pearls dressed in warm honey and colourful sprinkles.
steps: Knead flour, eggs, butter, sugar and zest; rest 25 minutes.
Roll into thin ropes and cut small nuggets.
Fry in batches at roughly 170°C until golden, then drain.
Coat in gently warmed honey and decorate in a wreath.
tip: Avoid overcrowding the frying pan.

name: Panforte di Siena
story: Dense Tuscan festive cake of nuts, candied peel, honey and spices.
steps: Toast and roughly chop the nuts.
Combine nuts, peel, flour and spices.
Warm honey with sugar, mix everything and press into a lined tin.
Bake at 150°C for 25–30 minutes; cool before slicing.
tip: Keep airtight and serve in small, rich wedges.

name: Ricciarelli
story: Siena’s soft almond sweets, delicately cracked beneath white icing sugar.
steps: Mix almonds with sugar and zest, then fold in egg whites and essence.
Chill for 30 minutes; shape oval biscuits.
Dust generously in icing sugar.
Bake at 155°C for 15–18 minutes and let cool fully.
tip: The centre should stay soft.

name: Tortellini in Brodo
story: Small filled pasta served in fragrant clear chicken or capon broth.
steps: Mince pork and cured meats finely and mix with cheese, egg and nutmeg.
Cut pasta squares and fill, folding into tortellini.
Bring broth to a gentle simmer.
Cook the pasta in broth for 3–5 minutes, until tender, then serve.
tip: Keep the filling cold while assembling.

name: Lasagne al Forno
story: Layers of pasta, beef ragù and béchamel for Christmas lunch.
steps: Soften chopped vegetables, brown beef and simmer with tomato for 45–60 minutes.
Layer pasta, ragù, béchamel and cheese in a deep baking dish.
Repeat to fill, ending with béchamel and cheese.
Bake at 180°C for 35–45 minutes and rest before cutting.
tip: Check whether your pasta sheets need preboiling.

name: Baccalà al Forno
story: Salt cod roasted with potatoes, olives and tomatoes, inspired by Christmas Eve traditions.
steps: Desalt cod beforehand as instructed by the fishmonger.
Roast sliced potatoes, onion and tomatoes with oil at 190°C for 20 minutes.
Add cod and olives, and roast 20–25 minutes more until fish flakes.
Finish with parsley and lemon; salt only if needed.
tip: Salt cod can remain quite salty.

name: Cartellate
story: Puglian rose-shaped fried pastries dipped in vincotto or honey.
steps: Knead flour, oil, wine or water and salt; rest 30 minutes.
Roll thin strips and coil into rosette shapes.
Fry at around 170°C until lightly golden; drain.
Dip in warm vincotto or honey.
tip: Handmade shapes need not be identical.

name: Bibingka
story: Banana-leaf-scented rice cake warmly associated with Simbang Gabi.
steps: Line a small tin with banana leaves or baking paper; heat oven to 190°C.
Mix rice flour, sugar, baking powder, eggs, coconut milk and butter.
Pour into tin and top with cheese or salted egg if desired.
Bake 25–30 minutes, brush with butter and serve with coconut.
tip: Use fine rice flour for a tender result.

name: Puto Bumbong — Home Style
story: Purple steamed rice delicacy finished with coconut, muscovado and butter.
ingredients: 50 g purple rice flour or ube colouring
steps: Add water gradually to the flour until moist and crumbly.
Pack into a suitable steaming mould lined with muslin.
Steam for 8–12 minutes until cooked.
Serve hot with butter, grated coconut and muscovado.
tip: The classic version is steamed in bamboo tubes.

name: Leche Flan
story: Glossy caramel custard that is a Filipino holiday favourite.
steps: Melt sugar to an amber caramel and coat the base of a mould.
Combine yolks, milks and vanilla gently; strain over caramel.
Cover and steam gently or bake in a water bath at 160°C for 40–55 minutes.
Cool and refrigerate thoroughly before unmoulding.
tip: Gentle heat prevents a bubbly custard.

name: Hamon with Pineapple Glaze
story: Sweet-savoury Noche Buena ham, often shared with queso de bola.
steps: Heat the oven to 165°C and place the cooked ham in a roasting dish.
Simmer juice, sugar, honey and mustard into a glaze.
Brush ham and heat covered, basting regularly.
Uncover briefly to caramelise; rest before slicing.
tip: Raw ham requires a different cooking procedure; check the label.

name: Pancit Bihon
story: Rice noodles tossed with colourful vegetables and chicken for a family feast.
steps: Soak noodles according to the packet.
Cook aromatics and chicken thoroughly, then add sliced vegetables.
Add stock and soy sauce, then toss in noodles until liquid is absorbed.
Serve hot with calamansi wedges.
tip: Add broth gradually because noodles absorb different amounts.

name: Lumpiang Shanghai
story: Crispy small spring rolls with savoury minced pork filling.
steps: Mix the pork, vegetables, soy sauce and egg.
Roll narrow portions in wrappers and seal tightly.
Fry in batches at 170°C until crisp and fully cooked inside.
Drain and serve with a sweet chilli dip.
tip: Cook a little filling first to check seasoning.

name: Pork Morcon
story: Festive pork roulade with a colourful filling of sausage, egg and vegetables.
steps: Marinate pork in soy and lemon for 30 minutes.
Lay sausage, eggs, carrot and pickles on the meat; roll and tie.
Brown the roll, then gently simmer in tomato sauce until tender and fully cooked.
Rest, remove twine and slice into rounds.
tip: Some households also prepare beef versions.

name: Creamy Fruit Salad
story: Chilled, creamy fruit salad is a colourful Christmas buffet classic.
steps: Drain the canned fruit very well.
Combine fruit, nata de coco and kaong.
Fold in cream and condensed milk; add diced cheese if preferred.
Chill for at least two hours and keep refrigerated.
tip: Keep dairy desserts cold during long gatherings.

name: Embutido
story: Steamed meatloaf that reveals eggs and sausage when cut into festive slices.
steps: Mix minced pork, grated carrot, onion, raw eggs, crumbs and relish.
Flatten on greased foil, add eggs and sausage and roll tightly.
Steam 45–60 minutes, ensuring meat is fully cooked.
Cool slightly, unwrap and slice; optionally pan-brown.
tip: Refrigerate prepared leftovers promptly.

name: Queso de Bola Holiday Platter
story: The famous red-waxed cheese becomes an easy Noche Buena platter.
steps: Completely remove the red wax and cut cheese into wedges.
Arrange cheese, cooked ham and bread attractively.
Add grapes, crackers and optional chutney.
Serve cool and refrigerate leftovers promptly.
tip: An assembled serving idea rather than a cooked dish.

name: German Christstollen
story: German enriched fruit bread with almonds and a snowy sugar finish.
steps: Mix flour, yeast, sugar and milk, then knead in butter.
Fold in fruit, nuts and cinnamon; let rise until puffy.
Shape an oval, with marzipan in the centre if desired.
Bake at 175°C for 35–45 minutes; brush with butter and coat in icing sugar.
tip: Wrap overnight to deepen the flavour.

name: British Mince Pies
story: Buttery pastry bites with aromatic fruit mincemeat.
steps: Cut pastry rounds to line a muffin tin.
Spoon mincemeat into cases without overfilling.
Cover with pastry stars and brush with egg.
Bake at 190°C for 18–22 minutes until golden and dust when cool.
tip: Check fillings for alcohol or animal suet if avoiding them.

name: French Bûche de Noël
story: Chocolate sponge roll decorated like a Christmas log.
steps: Whisk eggs and sugar; fold in flour and cocoa, then bake a thin sponge at 180°C for 10–12 minutes.
Roll warm sponge in parchment and cool.
Unroll, spread with whipped cream and reroll.
Coat in chocolate ganache and mark bark lines.
tip: Use edible decorations only.

name: Gingerbread Cookies
story: Spiced star and tree biscuits, lovely for decorating or gifting.
steps: Cream butter and sugar, beat in syrup and egg.
Mix in flour, spices and soda; chill for 30 minutes.
Roll thin and cut festive shapes.
Bake at 175°C for 9–12 minutes; decorate after cooling.
tip: Bake a little less for softer centres.

name: Mexican Christmas Tamales
story: Corn-husk parcels stuffed with chicken and chile sauce.
steps: Beat shortening; add masa, baking powder and warm stock for a spreadable dough.
Mix cooked shredded chicken with sauce.
Spread masa onto husks, add filling and fold closed.
Steam upright 60–90 minutes until the dough releases from the husk.
tip: Rest ten minutes before opening.

name: Australian Summer Pavlova
story: Crisp meringue topped with cream and bright fruit for a summery Christmas.
steps: Whisk whites to soft peaks, gradually add sugar, then cornflour and vinegar.
Shape a round meringue with a shallow centre.
Bake at 120°C for 75–90 minutes; cool in the oven.
Top with whipped cream and fresh fruit just before serving.
tip: Moisture softens crisp meringue; assemble at the last minute.

name: Polish Cabbage & Mushroom Pierogi
story: Tender dumplings filled with cabbage and mushrooms, a popular Christmas Eve option.
steps: Knead flour, water and oil; rest for 25 minutes.
Sauté onion and mushrooms and cook with drained sauerkraut until dry.
Roll pastry circles, fill and seal edges.
Boil until floating and cooked through, then dress with onions.
tip: Make sure the filling is not too wet.

name: Herb-Roast Christmas Turkey
story: A centrepiece for many North American holiday meals.
steps: Heat oven to 165°C; pat turkey dry and rub in seasoned herb butter.
Place turkey over vegetables in a roasting dish, adding stock as needed.
Roast until the thickest breast and thigh parts reach 74°C (165°F) using a food thermometer.
Rest 20 minutes before carving.
tip: Use a thermometer, not elapsed time alone.

name: Cappelletti in Brodo
story: Small filled pasta from Emilia-Romagna, often served in Christmas broth.
steps: Mix ricotta with Parmigiano and nutmeg.
Cut pasta into little squares and add a spoon of filling.
Fold into cappelletti, sealing the edges firmly.
Simmer in broth until pasta is cooked through.
tip: Keep the filled pasta covered to avoid drying.

name: Torrone
story: Italian nougat with honey and toasted nuts, familiar at Christmas fairs.
steps: Toast nuts and line a tin with wafer paper.
Heat honey and sugar carefully to the soft-ball stage.
Beat whites and gradually blend in hot syrup, following safe sugar-handling practices.
Fold in nuts, spread firmly and let set before cutting.
tip: Hot sugar syrup can cause severe burns.

name: Mostaccioli
story: Dark, spiced Italian Christmas biscuits often covered with chocolate.
steps: Mix flour, cocoa, baking powder and orange zest.
Work in honey and sugar until a stiff dough forms.
Shape diamonds and bake at 175°C for 12–15 minutes.
Cool and dip in melted chocolate.
tip: Allow the chocolate coating to harden completely.

name: Cotechino con Lenticchie
story: A favourite Italian New Year holiday dish pairing rich sausage with lentils.
steps: Simmer lentils with chopped vegetables and bay until tender.
Heat cotechino according to its package directions.
Slice the sausage and arrange over warm lentils.
Season with oil and pepper before serving.
tip: Traditionally associated especially with New Year's Eve.

name: Roccocò
story: Neapolitan ring biscuits with almonds and warming winter spices.
steps: Mix flour, sugar, nuts, zest and spices.
Add enough water for a firm dough.
Shape into small rings, brush with egg and bake at 180°C for 18–22 minutes.
Cool before storing.
tip: Traditionally crunchy; soften by dipping in a warm drink.

name: Polenta e Baccalà
story: Soft polenta with tender salt cod, especially fitting for winter gatherings.
steps: Make polenta in salted boiling water according to packet.
Sauté onion in olive oil and add tomatoes.
Add the desalted cod and cook gently until it flakes.
Serve cod sauce over warm polenta.
tip: Adjust salt only after tasting the cod.

name: Zelten
story: A festive fruit-and-nut cake from Trentino-Alto Adige.
steps: Soak and chop dried fruit.
Mix eggs, sugar and milk; fold in flour and baking powder.
Add fruit, nuts and zest, spread in a lined tin.
Bake at 175°C for 40–50 minutes.
tip: Different valleys use very different Zelten recipes.

name: Broccoli di Natale
story: A southern Italian Christmas side of greens with garlic, olive oil and citrus.
steps: Steam broccoli until just tender.
Warm sliced garlic gently in oil.
Toss broccoli with fragrant oil and lemon.
Finish with chilli if desired and serve warm.
tip: Avoid overcooking to keep the greens vivid.

name: Ube Halaya
story: Silky purple-yam jam beloved in Filipino desserts and holiday sharing.
steps: Combine ube, coconut milk and condensed milk in a heavy pan.
Cook slowly with constant stirring to prevent scorching.
Work in butter and stir until thick and glossy.
Transfer to a dish and cool before serving.
tip: Use genuine ube for its characteristic flavour.

name: Kutsinta
story: Chewy steamed Filipino rice cakes topped with freshly grated coconut.
ingredients: Food-grade lye water according to recipe
steps: Mix the flours, sugar and water to make a smooth batter.
Add only food-grade lye water in the small quantity directed on its label, or use a reliable lye-free formulation.
Pour into greased small moulds.
Steam 20–30 minutes until set; cool and top with coconut.
tip: Never substitute household chemical lye for food-grade ingredients.

name: Sapin-Sapin
story: Colourful layered rice-and-coconut cake for the Christmas buffet.
steps: Mix rice flour, coconut milk, water and sugar.
Divide batter and flavour portions with ube and pandan.
Steam each thin layer until just set before adding the next.
Cool completely and serve with toasted coconut.
tip: Grease the pan lightly for clean layers.

name: Buko Pandan
story: Creamy coconut-and-pandan dessert with jelly, young coconut and condensed milk.
steps: Prepare pandan jelly according to the packet and allow it to set.
Cut jelly into cubes and combine with coconut and nata de coco.
Fold in cream and condensed milk.
Chill thoroughly before serving.
tip: Reduce condensed milk if the coconut is already sweet.

name: Chicken Afritada
story: Comforting Filipino tomato-braised chicken with potatoes, carrots and peppers.
steps: Brown chicken lightly and remove.
Cook garlic and onion, then add tomato and return chicken.
Simmer gently until chicken is thoroughly cooked.
Add potatoes, carrots and peppers until tender.
tip: Check chicken doneness with a thermometer.

name: Beef Caldereta
story: Festive slow-braised beef with tomato, peppers and potatoes.
steps: Brown beef and sauté aromatics.
Add sauce, bay leaf and water, then simmer until beef tender.
Add potatoes, carrot and pepper.
Stir in liver spread if used; simmer until vegetables soften.
tip: Gentle braising gives the most tender result.

name: Pancit Malabon
story: Rich rice noodles with seafood, vibrant sauce and festive garnishes.
steps: Cook noodles separately and drain.
Sauté garlic and seafood until cooked; set aside.
Simmer stock with annatto and seasoning, then toss with noodles.
Top with seafood, hard-boiled eggs and spring onions.
tip: Check for shellfish and egg allergens.

name: Cassava Cake
story: A classic baked Filipino coconut-and-cassava dessert.
steps: Mix grated cassava, coconut milk, some condensed milk, butter and eggs.
Pour into a greased baking dish and bake at 180°C until nearly set.
Combine remaining condensed and evaporated milk as topping.
Bake again until golden and fully cooked.
tip: Use edible, correctly prepared cassava.

name: Maja Blanca
story: Coconut-milk pudding traditionally cut into squares and topped with toasted coconut.
steps: Dissolve cornflour in a little cool coconut milk.
Heat remaining milk with sugar, then gradually whisk in slurry.
Stir constantly until thick; fold in corn.
Pour into dish, cool, then top with toasted coconut.
tip: Avoid stopping the stirring while the pudding thickens.

name: Swedish Lussekatter
story: Golden saffron buns with raisins, associated with Saint Lucia in Sweden.
steps: Warm milk with saffron and dissolve yeast in it once lukewarm.
Knead flour, sugar, butter and milk into dough; let rise.
Shape S-shaped buns and add raisins.
Brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 10–12 minutes.
tip: Keep the dough soft, not stiff.

name: Spanish Turrón de Alicante
story: Crunchy Spanish almond-and-honey nougat enjoyed at Christmas.
steps: Line a tin with edible wafer paper.
Cook honey and sugar carefully into syrup.
Beat egg white and gradually blend with hot syrup.
Fold in nuts, press flat and let set before slicing.
tip: Sugar syrup is extremely hot; handle carefully.

name: Greek Melomakarona
story: Greek honey-dipped orange-and-spice Christmas cookies.
steps: Mix olive oil, orange juice, sugar and flour with spices.
Shape small ovals, mark tops and bake at 180°C for 22 minutes.
Warm honey with a little water and dip warm cookies briefly.
Scatter with chopped walnuts.
tip: Do not soak cookies too long or they may crumble.

name: Norwegian Krumkake
story: Delicate patterned wafer cookies rolled into elegant cones.
steps: Whisk eggs and sugar, then mix in butter, flour and cardamom.
Heat a krumkake iron and add a spoon of batter.
Cook until golden, according to iron instructions.
Roll immediately into cones and cool crisp.
tip: The wafers become brittle as they cool.

name: Puerto Rican Coquito
story: Creamy coconut-based festive drink; this family version is non-alcoholic.
steps: Blend all milks and coconut cream until smooth.
Add vanilla and spices.
Chill thoroughly for at least two hours.
Shake before serving over ice.
tip: This recipe omits rum and is suitable for a family celebration.

name: Ukrainian Kutia
story: Ceremonial sweet wheat-berry dish for Ukrainian Christmas Eve.
steps: Cook soaked wheat berries in water until tender.
Soften poppy seeds in hot water and drain.
Mix wheat with poppy seeds, raisins, nuts and honey.
Adjust with a little cooking liquid and chill or serve cool.
tip: Cooking time for wheat berries varies widely.

name: German Lebkuchen
story: Spiced German Christmas biscuits enriched with honey and nuts.
steps: Warm honey and sugar, then cool slightly.
Mix with remaining ingredients to form a dough.
Chill and form small rounds.
Bake at 175°C for 12–15 minutes, then glaze if desired.
tip: Resting the dough enhances flavour.

name: French Gratin Dauphinois
story: Velvety French potato gratin suitable as a Christmas side dish.
steps: Slice potatoes thinly and preheat the oven to 170°C.
Rub the baking dish with garlic and butter.
Layer potatoes with seasoned milk and cream.
Bake 60–75 minutes until tender and golden.
tip: Traditional versions do not always include cheese.

name: Japanese Christmas Strawberry Shortcake
story: Light sponge, whipped cream and strawberries are a festive Japanese favourite.
steps: Beat eggs and sugar until thick, then fold in flour and butter.
Bake at 175°C for 25–30 minutes, cool and split into layers.
Brush lightly with syrup and fill with whipped cream and sliced berries.
Cover with cream, decorate and chill.
tip: Keep chilled because the cake contains fresh cream.

name: Tiramisù
story: Coffee-soaked sponge fingers and mascarpone cream; a much-loved Italian celebration dessert.
steps: Beat pasteurised egg yolks and sugar until thick and mix in mascarpone.
Fold in separately beaten pasteurised whites.
Dip biscuits quickly in coffee and layer with cream.
Chill for at least four hours and dust with cocoa.
tip: Use pasteurised eggs for no-bake preparation.

name: Cannoli Siciliani
story: Crisp Sicilian pastry tubes filled with sweetened ricotta.
steps: Drain ricotta and beat with sugar and zest until smooth.
Fold in chocolate chips.
Fill cannoli shells just before serving.
Dip ends in pistachios or decorate with candied peel.
tip: Keep shells separate until the last moment.

name: Arancini di Riso
story: Golden rice croquettes with a fragrant ragù and cheese filling.
steps: Cook rice in stock and cool until firm.
Wrap spoonfuls of rice around ragù and mozzarella.
Dip in egg and roll in breadcrumbs.
Fry at 170°C until deeply golden and heated through.
tip: Chill shaped arancini before frying.

name: Zabaglione
story: Airy custard made by whisking egg yolks over gentle heat, served with Christmas biscuits.
steps: Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl.
Gradually add Marsala or grape juice.
Set over barely simmering water and whisk continuously until thick and safely heated.
Serve warm in small glasses.
tip: Avoid boiling the egg mixture.

name: Risotto alla Milanese
story: Golden saffron risotto that brings elegance to a winter celebration.
steps: Soften finely chopped onion in butter.
Toast rice and gradually add hot stock, stirring.
Infuse saffron in stock and add partway through.
Finish creamy with butter and Parmigiano.
tip: Serve immediately for the best texture.

name: Frittelle di Mele
story: Apple slices in a light golden batter with cinnamon sugar.
steps: Peel and core apples and cut rings.
Whisk flour, egg, milk and baking powder into batter.
Dip apple rings and fry at 170°C until golden.
Drain and roll lightly in cinnamon sugar.
tip: Dry the apples well before battering.

name: Chicken Adobo
story: Chicken simmered in soy, vinegar, garlic and bay leaves; a Filipino family favourite.
steps: Brown the chicken lightly.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, garlic, bay, peppercorns and water.
Simmer uncovered until chicken is safely cooked and sauce has reduced.
Serve over steamed rice.
tip: Taste before adding any salt.

name: Sinigang na Baboy
story: Tamarind-sour pork soup with tender vegetables.
steps: Simmer pork with onion and tomatoes until tender.
Add radish and string beans; cook until just soft.
Season gradually with tamarind to taste.
Stir in leafy greens and finish briefly.
tip: Adjust the sourness to your family preference.

name: Kare-Kare
story: Rich Filipino peanut stew, often served with vegetables and shrimp paste on the side.
steps: Simmer beef until tender, reserving its broth.
Sauté garlic, onion and annatto; add broth and peanut butter.
Add beef and vegetables, simmering until cooked.
Serve with rice and optional shrimp paste separately.
tip: Contains peanut allergen; shrimp paste contains shellfish.

name: Halo-Halo
story: Layered shaved-ice dessert with sweet beans, fruit, jellies and milk.
steps: Divide chilled beans, fruits and jellies among glasses.
Pile on fresh shaved ice.
Pour milk around the ice.
Top with ube halaya and optional leche flan.
tip: Serve immediately before the ice melts.

name: Ensaymada
story: Soft buttery sweet bread coils finished with sugar and grated cheese.
steps: Knead flour, yeast, milk, eggs and sugar until elastic.
Add butter gradually and let rise until doubled.
Shape coiled buns and let rise again.
Bake at 175°C for 15–20 minutes, brush with butter and add cheese and sugar.
tip: A soft dough gives the buns their signature texture.

name: Puto Cheese
story: Small steamed Filipino rice cakes topped with cheese.
steps: Mix flour, sugar and baking powder.
Beat in milk, egg and melted butter.
Fill greased small moulds two-thirds full.
Steam 12–15 minutes and add a cheese sliver near the end.
tip: Keep the steam gentle to avoid collapsing.

name: Lechon
story: Crisp roasted pork is a lavish feast centrepiece in many Filipino celebrations.
steps: Score and dry the pork skin thoroughly.
Season meat with garlic, lemongrass, salt and pepper.
Roast at moderate heat until the meat is safely cooked.
Finish at higher heat to crisp the skin; rest before cutting.
tip: This is a home-oven pork belly adaptation of whole-pig lechon.

name: Christmas Pudding
story: Steamed British winter pudding packed with fruit and spice.
steps: Mix dried fruit, dry ingredients and grated butter.
Beat in eggs and zest.
Pack into a well-greased pudding basin and cover securely.
Steam gently for 3 hours, topping up water as needed.
tip: Let cool before unmoulding and reheating.

name: Eggnog — Non-Alcoholic
story: Creamy, nutmeg-scented holiday drink for the whole family.
steps: Whisk yolks with sugar until creamy.
Warm milk and cream with nutmeg and vanilla.
Gradually temper yolks with warm milk and heat gently until safely cooked.
Cool thoroughly and refrigerate.
tip: Use pasteurised eggs if serving without fully cooked custard.

name: Potato Latkes
story: Crisp potato pancakes enjoyed during Hanukkah.
steps: Grate potato and onion; squeeze out liquid.
Mix with eggs, flour and seasoning.
Fry spoonfuls in shallow oil until golden on both sides.
Drain and serve with applesauce or sour cream.
tip: An overlapping winter holiday tradition, not specifically Christmas.

name: American Pecan Pie
story: A rich nut pie served through the American holiday season.
steps: Line a pie tin with pastry and chill.
Whisk eggs, sugar, syrup, butter and vanilla.
Scatter pecans in shell and pour filling over.
Bake at 175°C for 45–55 minutes until just set.
tip: Cool before slicing to let filling firm up.

name: Roast Beef with Yorkshire Pudding
story: A British-style roast dinner with crisp, airy Yorkshire puddings.
steps: Season and roast beef until it reaches your desired safe doneness; rest.
Whisk flour, eggs and milk into a smooth batter.
Heat a little fat in a muffin tin until very hot.
Pour batter into tin and bake at 220°C for 20–25 minutes without opening oven.
tip: Use a meat thermometer to check doneness.

name: Baklava
story: Layers of flaky pastry, nuts and fragrant syrup enjoyed across many cultures.
steps: Layer filo sheets with butter and walnuts in a baking tin.
Cut diamonds before baking.
Bake at 180°C for 35–45 minutes until golden.
Pour cooled honey syrup over hot pastry and leave to absorb.
tip: Keep filo covered while working to prevent drying.

name: Hot Chocolate
story: Thick winter cocoa topped with whipped cream or marshmallows.
steps: Heat milk gently in a saucepan.
Whisk in cocoa, sugar and chopped chocolate until smooth.
Add vanilla and warm through without boiling.
Serve in mugs with optional cream.
tip: Use good-quality dark chocolate for depth.
